newsitem.title: INDIA: Paribas ups India Ranbaxy 96/97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Paribas ups India Ranbaxy 96/97 earnings.

text.p: Securities firm Paribas Capital Markets said on Tuesday it raised its earnings forecast for Ranbaxy Laboratories after the Indian pharmaceutical firm's recent acquisitions.
Paribas analyst Rupa Bose said she raised Ranbaxy's earnings per share (EPS) forecast to 31 rupees from 27.9 rupees for the financial year ended March 31, 1997.

"We think Ranbaxy's recent moves in India to acquire Croslands, a pharmaceutical company, and buy out the brands of drug company Gufic, signal a renewed interest in strengthening its Indian base," Bose said in a note to investors.
Ranbaxy's main investments recently have been overseas but last month the firm said it had acquired niche player Croslands Research Labs and bought the brands of drug firm Gufic.
Bose said her revised net profit forecast for Ranbaxy was 1.56 billion rupees against a previous estimate of 1.4 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March).
"Critics will carp that the company will over-extend itself -- financially and managerially. We disagree," Bose said.
She said Ranbaxy was bound to need funds over the next few years as it continued to expand and as its overseas businesses started requiring more working capital.
"Ranbaxy still has a reasonable gearing, though, and its subsidiaries are beginning to source their working capital needs locally," Bose said.
She said in the short term, the company was likely to face the usual integration issues following a merger.
"The company is sensitive to the issues involved, and an integration team is actively working to ensure that the process goes smoothly," Bose said.
